message.content: The Milwaukee Bucks won the 2021 NBA Finals, defeating the Phoenix Suns in six games [4]. This victory marked the Bucks' first championship since 1971 [4]. Giannis Antetokounmpo was named Finals MVP [4].

passages.heading: Los Angeles Lakers
passages.text: The Lakers clinched their first playoff berth since the 2012–13 season in March 2020, days before the season was suspended.<sup>[19]</sup><sup>[20]</sup> It ended the longest drought in the franchise's history.<sup>[20]</sup> After play resumed in the bubble, the Lakers clinched both their first Pacific Division title since 2012 and the top seed in the Western Conference playoffs for the first time since the 2009–10 season.<sup>[21]</sup> James and Davis were runner-ups for the NBA Most Valuable Player and NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award, respectively, behind Giannis Antetokounmpo, and both were named to the All-NBA First Team.<sup>[22]</sup>

passages.heading: Game 6
passages.text: With the Dodgers winning the World Series later in the month, Los Angeles repeated its achievement of having NBA and World Series champions in the same year, as both the Lakers and Dodgers had won in 1988.

passages.heading: Champions
passages.text:
## Champions

[edit]
The most recent champions are the New York Knicks, who won their first championship since 1973. The Boston Celtics have won the most championships of any team in the league at 18.<sup>[5]</sup> As of 2026<sup>[update]</sup>, the Eastern champions have a 42–38 advantage in NBA titles over the Western champions. The 1949–50 Minneapolis Lakers, who won the NBA Finals, are counted in the Eastern versus Western champions record as they played that sole season in the Central Division before returning to the Western Division.

- The first parentheses in the *Western champions* and*Eastern champions* columns indicate the teams' playoff seed. The second parentheses indicate the number of times that teams have appeared in an NBA Finals as well as each respective team's NBA Finals record to date.

# NBA Champions by Year: Complete list of NBA Finals winners

The __NBA__ Finals are chock-full of history and iconic moments. We've seen legendary franchises, like the Boston Celtics and Los Angeles Lakers, dominate the league, as well as newer powerhouses like the Golden State Warriors and Miami Heat. This year, Jalen Brunson and the New York Knicks defeated Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs for their first title in 53 years.

Let's take a look back at the complete list of NBA Finals winners.

passages.heading: **Which teams have won the most NBA championships?**
passages.text:
### **Which teams have won the most NBA championships?**

The Celtics have the most NBA titles with 18. Here’s a list of teams that have won at least three NBA championships:

- Boston Celtics (18 titles)
- Los Angeles Lakers (17)
- Golden State Warriors (7)
- Chicago Bulls (6)
- San Antonio Spurs (5)
- Philadelphia 76ers (3)
- Detroit Pistons (3)
- Miami Heat (3)

passages.heading: **Which teams have never won an NBA championship?**
passages.text:
### **Which teams have never won an NBA championship?**

Ten NBA franchises have never won an NBA Finals:

- Brooklyn Nets
- Charlotte Hornets
- Indiana Pacers
- Los Angeles Clippers
- Memphis Grizzlies
- Minnesota Timberwolves
- New Orleans Pelicans
- Orlando Magic
- Phoenix Suns
- Utah Jazz
